easy.def: A small egg-shaped toy you blow into to make music.

more.def: A small musical instrument shaped like an egg that you blow into.
examples: He played a tune on the ocarina.
The ocarina made a sweet, soft sound.
My birthday is a special occasion.
We wear nice clothes on special occasions.

more.def: A particular time when something happens, or a special event.
examples: A birthday is a special occasion.
On one occasion, we saw a deer in the yard.
We wear nice clothes for special occasions.
We have an occasional rainy day.

more.def: Happening only some of the time; not often.
examples: We have an occasional rainy day in the summer.
An occasional visitor stopped by the old farm.

more.def: Now and then, but not often.
examples: I occasionally eat cake on weekends.
We occasionally go to the movies.
It occasionally snows here in spring.

easy.def: A person who is in a place.

more.def: A person who lives in or is using a place or seat.
examples: The occupant of the house waved from the window.
Each occupant of the car wore a seat belt.
A nest's occupant was a small brown wren.
A teacher's occupation is to teach.

more.def: A person's job or the work that they do.
examples: A nurse's occupation is to take care of sick people.
We learned about different occupations on career day.
His occupation is a farmer, and he grows corn and beans.

easy.def: Having to do with a job.

more.def: Having to do with a person's job or work.
examples: Sore feet are an occupational problem for waiters.
The company teaches occupational safety to its workers.
The school held an occupational fair where people talked about their jobs.

easy.def: To take up a space or time.

more.def: To take up space or time, or to live in a place.
examples: The big couch occupies half the room.
A new family occupied the house next door.
Puzzles occupied the kids all afternoon.

more.def: To take place or happen, often without warning.
examples: The eclipse will occur on Tuesday.
Storms often occur in the late afternoon.
A good idea occurred to her while she was walking.

more.def: Something that happens; an event.
examples: Rain is a common occurrence in spring.
A comet is a rare occurrence in the night sky.
The strange occurrence made everyone talk.

easy.def: A very big sea of salt water.

more.def: One of the huge bodies of salt water that cover most of the Earth.
examples: The Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean in the world.
Sea turtles travel across the ocean to lay eggs.
From the plane, the ocean looked endless.

more.def: Having to do with the ocean.
examples: Oceanic waters cover most of the planet.
The ship made an oceanic voyage.

easy.def: A scientist who studies the sea.

more.def: A scientist who studies the oceans and the life in them.
examples: The oceanographer studied the deep sea.
An oceanographer measures waves and tides.
She works on a ship as an oceanographer.

more.def: The science that studies the oceans and the life in them.
examples: Oceanography teaches about waves and tides.
The oceanography class visited a research ship.

easy.def: A small wild cat with spots.
examples: An ocelot is a wild cat.

more.def: A wild cat of Central and South America with a spotted coat.
examples: An ocelot crept through the jungle.
The ocelot has a spotted, golden coat.

more.def: A yellow-brown color, or the earthy mineral that makes it.
examples: The wall was painted a warm ochre.
The vase was a deep ochre.
A stop sign is an octagon.

more.def: A flat shape with eight straight sides.
examples: A stop sign has the shape of an octagon.
An octagon has eight sides and eight angles.

more.def: Having eight straight sides.
examples: They sat at an octagonal table.
The tower had an octagonal room.

easy.def: A shape with eight triangle sides.

more.def: A solid shape with eight faces that are triangles.
examples: An octahedron has eight triangle faces.
It looks like two pyramids stuck together, an octahedron.
We built an octahedron from sticks.

easy.def: A set of eight musical notes.

more.def: The distance in music between one note and the next note with the same name, eight notes higher or lower.
examples: She sang a scale that covered one octave.
A piano has more than seven octaves.
The singer's voice rose by an octave.

more.def: A group of eight singers or players, or a piece of music for eight.
examples: The octet sang at the concert.

more.def: The tenth month of the year, when leaves change color in many places.
examples: We carve pumpkins at the end of October.
October brings crisp air and bright red leaves.

easy.def: A sea animal with eight arms.
examples: We saw an octopus at the aquarium.

more.def: A soft-bodied sea animal with eight long arms and a round head that can squirt ink to escape from enemies.
examples: The octopus squirted a cloud of ink and swam away.
An octopus has eight arms with rows of suckers.
The clever octopus opened the jar to get the crab inside.
